Preparation of standard solution of sodium carbonate.

We require 250ml standard flask, 250ml conical flask, solid sodium carbonate, hydrochloric acid (HCl), methyl orange, weighing bottle, electronic balance, funnel, glass rod, burette, 20ml pipette etc.
Take a weighing bottle.
Place it on an electronic balance.
Tare the balance.
Take a small amount of sodium carbonate using a spatula.
Transfer the sodium carbonate into the weighing bottle.
Weigh about 2.65g of sodium carbonate.
Remove the weighing bottle from the balance.
Carefully transfer theweighed quantity of sodium carbonate into a 250ml beaker.Wash the weighing bottle with distilled water.
Pour the washings into the beaker (Repeat this process 2 0r 3 times.). Gently stir the contents in the beaker using a clean glass rod till the sodium carbonate gets dissolved.
Transfer the entire solution from the beaker into a 250ml standard flask using a funnel and a glass rod.
Transfer the entire solution from the beaker into a 250ml standard flask using a funnel and a glass rod.
Wash the beaker 2 to 3 times with distilled water.
Transfer the washings into the standard flask and wash the glass rod as well.

Finally wash the funnel and funnel tip thoroughly with distilled water to transfer the solution sticking in the funnel to the standard flask. Using the wash bottle, carefully add distilled water to the standard flask to just below its calibration mark.
Using a clean pipette,Pipette out a small volume of distilled water.
Take the standard flask.
Take the standard flask.
notext
Add last few drops of distilled water using the pipette until the lower level of the meniscus just touches the mark on the standard flask.
Add last few drops of distilled water using the pipette until the lower level of the meniscus just touches the mark on the standard flask.
Stopper the standard flask.
Shake gently to make the sodium carbonate solution uniform throughout.
The molarity of the prepared sodium carbonate solution is 0.1 M (0.1 molar).
Determination of strength of given hydrochloric acid using standard sodium carbonate solution.
Fix a clean burette to a burette stand and place a funnel over the mouth of the burette.
Take the bottle containing hydrochloric acid.
Pour a small amount of hydrochloric acid into the burette through the funnel.
Remove the funnel and take the burette from the stand.
Rinse the burette with hydrochloric acid to remove any moisture inside the burette.
Rinse the burette with hydrochloric acid to remove any moisture inside the burette.
Take the burette to the sink and open the stop-cock to drain out the washings from the burette.
Clamp the burette vertically in the burette stand and place the funnel over the mouth of the burette.
Then take hydrochloric acid.
Fill the burette with HCl just above the zero mark using the funnel.
Fill the burette with hydrochloric acid just above the zero mark using the funnel.
Place a beaker below the burette and slowly open the stop cock so that hydrochloric acid is allowed to run out into the beaker and set the initial burette reading as zero.
Place a beaker below the burette and slowly open the stop cock so that hydrochloric acid is allowed to run out into the beaker and set the initial burette reading as zero.
Place a beaker below the burette and slowly open the stop cock so that hydrochloric acid is allowed to run out into the beaker and set the initial burette reading as zero.

Pipette out a small volume of sodium carbonate solution.

Then rinse the pipette with sodium carbonate solution to remove any moisture inside the pipette.

Now pipette out the sodium carbonate solution from the standard flask until the solution level is just above the calibration mark on the pipette.
Now pipette out the sodium carbonate solution from the standard flask until the solution level is just above the calibration mark on the pipette.
Now pipette out the sodium carbonate solution from the standard flask until the solution level is just above the calibration mark on the pipette.

Close the open end of the pipette with index finger. Slowly release the finger so that the solution is allowed to run slowly until the lower edge of the meniscus just touches the calibration mark. The volume of the solution should become 20 ml.
Now transfer the 20ml sodium carbonate solution into a clean conical flask.
Touch the tip of the pipette with the bottom of the conical flask to transfer the remaining solution from the pipette.
Take a small quantity of methyl orange indicator.
Add two drops of methyl orange indicator into the conical flask.
The colour of the solution in the conical flask becomes yellow.
Place the conical flask on a white tile under the burette to correctly view the colour change.

Run the solution drop wise from the burette into the conical flask with constant shaking of the solution in the conical flask till the colour of the solution changes from yellow to light red on addition of last single drop of HCl.
Note down the final burette reading and repeat the same procedure until concordant values are obtained.
Record the observations on a tabular column.
Record the volume of sodium carbonate solution, molarity of sodium carbonate solution and volume of hydrochloric acid.
